# Preparations

Load the necessary libraries

```{r}
#| label: libraries
#| output: false
#| eval: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| cache: false

library(tidyverse)     #for data wrangling etc
library(cmdstanr)      #for cmdstan
library(brms)          #for fitting models in STAN
library(coda)          #for diagnostics
library(bayesplot)     #for diagnostics
library(DHARMa)        #for residual diagnostics
library(rstan)         #for interfacing with STAN
library(emmeans)       #for marginal means etc
library(broom)         #for tidying outputs
library(tidybayes)     #for more tidying outputs
library(ggeffects)     #for partial plots
library(broom.mixed)   #for summarising models

source("helperFunctions.R")
```

# Scenario

@Loyn-1987-1987 modelled the abundance of forest birds with six predictor
variables (patch area, distance to nearest patch, distance to nearest
larger patch, grazing intensity, altitude and years since the patch had
been isolated).

![Regent honeyeater](../resources/regent_honeyeater_small.jpg){#fig-honeyeater width="165" height="240"}


ABUND   DIST   LDIST   AREA   GRAZE   ALT   YR.ISOL
------- ------ ------- ------ ------- ----- ---------
..      ..     ..      ..     ..      ..    ..

: Format of loyn.csv data file {#tbl-loyn .table-condensed}

------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
**ABUND**     Abundance of forest birds in patch- response variable
**DIST**      Distance to nearest patch - predictor variable
**LDIST**     Distance to nearest larger patch - predictor variable
**AREA**      Size of the patch - predictor variable
**GRAZE**     Grazing intensity (1 to 5, representing light to heavy) - predictor variable
**ALT**       Altitude - predictor variable
**YR.ISOL**   Number of years since the patch was isolated - predictor variable
------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

: Description of the variables in the loyn data file {#tbl-loyn1 .table-condensed}

The aim of the analysis is to investigate the effects of a range of
predictors on the abundance of forest birds.

# Read in the data

```{r readData, results='markdown', eval=TRUE}
loyn <- read_csv('../data/loyn.csv', trim_ws=TRUE)

head(loyn)
#going to treat GRAZE as a categorical factor so we name it fGRAZE, keeping GRAZE in the dataset
loyn <- loyn |> 
  mutate(fGRAZE = factor(GRAZE))
```

# Exploratory data analysis

```{r}
#| label: check assuemptions for normal model
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

#put response first
scatterplotMatrix(~ABUND+DIST+LDIST+AREA+fGRAZE+ALT+YR.ISOL, data = loyn,
                  diagonal = list(method = 'boxplot'))
#diagonal has distribution for each
#abundance is on the top row
#the top row, second column is a y-axis of ABUND and x-axis of DIST

#if predictor is skewed, some of the other assumptions might not be met
#predictors can be transformed and messed with but don't want to do this for the response variable
#if transformations don't improve things, then leave the predictor alone (ex. YR.ISOL)

#need to address skewed DIST, LDIST, and AREA first
#transform with log
scatterplotMatrix(~ABUND+log(DIST)+log(LDIST)+log(AREA)+fGRAZE+ALT+YR.ISOL, data = loyn,
                  diagonal = list(method = 'boxplot'))
#box plots look much better!
#we are just looking for anything OBVIOUS
#seems like DIST and LDIST are correlated so might need to drop one of them
```

Model formula:
$$
\begin{align}
y_i &\sim{} \mathcal{N}(\mu_i, \sigma^2)\\
log(\mu_i) &= \boldsymbol{\beta} \bf{X_i}\\
\beta_0 &\sim{} \mathcal{N}(3.4, 0.1)\\
\beta_{1-9} &\sim{} \mathcal{N}(0, 2)\\
\sigma &\sim{} \mathcal{t}(3,0, 1.5)
\end{align}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is a vector of effects parameters and $\bf{X}$ is a model matrix representing the additive effects of
the scaled versions of distance (ln), distance to the nearest large patch (ln), patch area (ln), grazing intensity, year of isolation and
altitude on the abundance of forest birds.

```{r}
#| label: model formula
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

#a normal model gives negative bird predictions so need to try something else like a log normal distribution
#centering and scaling continuous predictors
loyn_form <- bf(ABUND ~ scale(log(LDIST)) +
                  scale(log(AREA)) +
                  fGRAZE +
                  scale(ALT) +
                  scale(YR.ISOL),
                family = gaussian(link = 'log')
                )

```


```{r}
#| label: priors
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn |> group_by(fGRAZE) |> 
  summarise(median(log(ABUND)),
            mad(log(ABUND)))

#intercept here is the avg number birds when all predictors are zero and graze = 1.
#it includes a mix of continuous and categorical predictors

get_prior(loyn_form, data = loyn)

priors <- prior(normal(3.4,0.1), class = 'Intercept') + #for SD just round the first one
  prior(normal(0,2), class = 'b') + #need to account for differences between 3.38 and 1.34 so maybe go with 2 
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1.1), class="sigma")


```

# Fit the model

```{r}
#| label: fit model
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| cache: true

loyn_brm2 <- brm(loyn_form,
                 data = loyn,
                 prior = priors,
                 sample_prior = 'only',
                 iter = 5000,
                 warmup = 1000,
                 chains = 3, cores = 3,
                 thin = 5,
                 refresh = 0,
                 backend = "cmdstanr",
                 seed = 1)

```

```{r}
#| label: conditional effect plot
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_brm2 |> 
  conditional_effects() |> 
  plot(points = TRUE, ask = FALSE, plot = FALSE) |> 
  wrap_plots() &
  scale_y_log10()

#the priors must be very wide
```

```{r}
#| label: model with priors and data
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_brm3 <- update(loyn_brm2, sample_prior = 'yes', refresh = 0)

loyn_brm3 |> 
  conditional_effects() |> 
  plot(points = TRUE, ask = FALSE, plot = FALSE) |> 
  wrap_plots() &
  scale_y_log10()

#fGRAZE 5 looks weird, the mean is way up high compared to the points
#could be sigma wasn't wide enough or the variance for slope of fGRAZE is too small

```

```{r}
#| label: try adjusting slope prior for fGRAZE
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

get_prior(loyn_form, data = loyn)

priors <- prior(normal(3.4,0.1), class = 'Intercept') + 
  prior(normal(0,2), class = 'b') + 
  prior(normal(0, 10), class = 'b', coef = "fGRAZE5") +
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1.1), class="sigma")

loyn_brm4 <- brm(loyn_form,
                 data = loyn,
                 prior = priors,
                 sample_prior = 'yes',
                 iter = 5000,
                 warmup = 1000,
                 chains = 3, cores = 3,
                 thin = 5,
                 refresh = 0,
                 backend = "cmdstanr",
                 seed = 1)

#these plots show y relative to x when all other predictors are accounted for
loyn_brm4 |> 
  conditional_effects() |> 
  plot(points = TRUE, ask = FALSE, plot = FALSE) |> 
  wrap_plots() &
  scale_y_log10()

#fGRAZE5 still looks the same :(
#so shrinkage is real and not an artifact of the model/priors

```

# MCMC sampling diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: examine all priors and posteriors
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_brm3 |> 
  SUYR_prior_and_posterior()

#prior for b was already so wide, making it larger in brm4 wouldn't have helped

#main thing to look for, you want posterior and prior to be different from each other
```

# Model validation

```{r}
#| label: model diagnostics
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_brm3$fit |> stan_trace(inc_warmup = TRUE)

loyn_brm3$fit |> stan_ac()

loyn_brm3$fit |> stan_rhat()

loyn_brm3$fit |> stan_ess()
```

```{r}
#| label: posterior probs density overlay
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_brm3 |> pp_check(type = 'dens_overlay', ndraws=100)

#dark line is actual distribution of our data
#our model reconstructs the data okayyy
```

```{r}
#| label: simulate residuals
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn.resids <- make_brms_dharma_res(loyn_brm3, integerResponse = TRUE)
testUniformity(loyn.resids)
plotResiduals(loyn.resids)
testDispersion(loyn.resids)

#to the right = overdispersion
#to the left = underdispersed

#model is being drama queen...its really all good
```

# Partial effects plots

```{r}
#| label: conditional effects plot again
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_brm3 |> 
  conditional_effects() |> 
  plot(points = TRUE, ask = FALSE, plot = FALSE) |> 
  wrap_plots() &
  scale_y_log10()
```

# Model investigation
```{r}
#| label: make summary table
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_brm3 |> 
  as_draws_df() |> 
  dplyr::select(matches("^b_.*|^sigma$")) |> 
  mutate(across(matches("^b_.*"), exp)) |> #just exp b's, doesn't make sense to do this for sigma
  summarise_draws(median, 
                  HDInterval::hdi,
                  rhat, 
                  ess_bulk,
                  Pl = ~mean(.x < 1), #less than 
                  Pg = ~mean(.x > 1)) #greater than

#23 is the expected number of birds in GRAZE1 when all other continuous variables are at their average (0) (aka holding all other predictors constant)

#for every one unit change in scalelogDIST the expected number of birds increases by 4% (median = 1.038)

#for every one unit change in scalelogAREA, the expected number of birds increases by 21% (median = 1.205). And there was strong evidence of a positive change.

#for medians below 1, you need to convert scale for comparisons (invert negatives)
#for GRAZE5
1/0.465 # = 2.15

#GRAZE5 has the biggest impact on bird abundance followed by AREA
```

# Further analyses

```{r}
#| label: habitat model
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

#area, grazing, and interaction
loyn_habitat <- update(loyn_brm3, .~scale(log(AREA)) *
                  fGRAZE, refresh = 0)

```

```{r}
#| label: connectivity model
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

#LDIST
loyn_connect <- update(loyn_brm3, .~scale(log(LDIST)), refresh = 0)

```

```{r}
#| label: climate model
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

#ALT
loyn_climate <- update(loyn_brm3, .~scale(ALT), refresh = 0)

```

```{r}
#| label: NULL model
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

#to assess the other models against
loyn_null <- update(loyn_brm3, .~1, refresh = 0) #1 signifies an intercept

```

```{r}
#| label: compare models
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loo_compare(loo(loyn_habitat), loo(loyn_null)) 
#habitat is 30x better than null. Is useful. Has an impact on bird abundance.

loo_compare(loo(loyn_connect), loo(loyn_null)) 
#null and connect are considered the same. The SE is large enough to encompass 0

loo_compare(loo(loyn_climate), loo(loyn_null))
#climate is 3.5x better than null. Is useful. Has an impact on bird abundance.
```

```{r}
#| label: plots
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_habitat |> 
  conditional_effects("AREA:fGRAZE") |> 
  plot(points = TRUE, ask = FALSE, plot = FALSE) |> 
  wrap_plots() &
  scale_y_log10() &
  scale_x_log10() &
  scale_fill_viridis_d() &
  scale_color_viridis_d()

```

```{r}
#| label: habitat table
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

#on fractional scale
loyn_habitat |> 
  as_draws_df() |> 
  dplyr::select(matches("^b_.*|^sigma$")) |> 
  mutate(across(matches("^b_.*"), exp)) |> #just exp b's, doesn't make sense to do this for sigma
  summarise_draws(median, 
                  HDInterval::hdi,
                  Pl = ~mean(.x < 1), #less than 
                  Pg = ~mean(.x > 1)) #greater than

#Intercept: the expected average abundance of birds is 26.4, in GRAZE1 when AREA = 0 (at the average AREA)

#GRAZE2: 15% lower abundance in GRAZE2 than GRAZE1 (1-0.865) at the average AREA

#for every unit change in AREA, bird abundance increases by 10%

#slopes are not equal for every GRAZE category. b_scalelogAREA:fGRAZE2 is 23% higher, b_scalelogAREA:fGRAZE3 is 27% higher, and so on. So ABUNDANCE depends on AREA and GRAZING
```

```{r}
#| label: label
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

newdata <- with(loyn, data.frame(AREA = c(min(AREA), mean(AREA), max(AREA))))

loyn_table <- loyn_habitat |> 
  emmeans(~fGRAZE | AREA, at = newdata, type = "response") |> #response back transforms
  pairs() |> 
  tidy_draws() |> 
  exp() |>  #need to undo logit scale because tidy_draws doesn't recognize response from above
  summarise_draws(median, 
                  HDInterval::hdi,
                  Pl = ~mean(.x < 1), #less than
                  Pg = ~mean(.x > 1), #greater than
                  ROPE = ~mean(.x > 0.9 & .x < 1.1)) # whats the probability that all the data is within 10% of 1

```

```{r}
#| label: compare slopes of each GRAZE
#| eval: true
#| echo: true

loyn_habitat |> 
  emtrends(~fGRAZE, var = "log(AREA)") |> 
  pairs()

#ones that don't include 0 are likely significant
```
